title: Design System: Nawres Ben Rhouma — Portfolio

terracotta.note: The only chromatic voice at text weight: links, the selected folder tab label, the current nav item, the hero rule, bullet markers, the Core status token, promoted hovers. 4.5:1 on the butter ground.

terracotta-fill.note: The same hue one step heavier, used only as a background behind white: the Get in touch button, the favicon rule. Never used as text.

burnt-terracotta.note: Hover state of the primary fill only.

espresso-ink.note: All body and heading text, and the secondary button's fill (View CV) with butter text on it.

butter-page.note: The page ground everywhere below the hero band.

deep-butter-band.note: The sticky header and the hero band: one tint step deeper so the first viewport reads as a plate the work sheet floats on.

warm-sheet.note: Every sheet, panel, note, theme toggle and the CV page. Off-white, never pure white.

butter-chip.note: The fill behind code chips only.

warm-brown-grey.note: Muted text: labels, dates, meta lines, unselected tabs and nav links, the footer.

butter-hairline.note: Every rule inside content (field rows, timeline, fact strips, column dividers, footer edge), and the dark theme's sheet edge.

control-hairline.note: 3.5:1 on the butter ground. Outlines of operable controls only: theme toggle, ghost button, status tokens, skip link, scrollbar.

roasted-ground-dark.note: Dark-theme page ground. Same role as butter-page.

roasted-sheet-dark.note: Dark-theme sheet, edged by a 1px roasted-hairline ring instead of a shadow.

cream-dark.note: Dark-theme text, and the secondary button's fill inverts to it automatically.

lit-terracotta-dark.note: Dark-theme accent at text weight, and the dark primary hover and focus ring. Same rules as terracotta.

lit-terracotta-fill-dark.note: Dark-theme primary button fill, with the roasted ground as its contrast colour.

roasted-hairline-dark.note: Dark-theme content rules, and the sheet's edge where the shadow token becomes a hairline ring.

display.purpose: The page h1 and the CV name. Gabarito 800 set tight at -0.03em, line-height 1.02. Once per page.

case-title.purpose: The selected-work panel title. Deliberately one step above the display size: the sheet owns the focal event of the first viewport.

headline.purpose: Section h2s, set as a baseline-aligned flex row so the # heading anchor sits beside them.

title.purpose: h3s. Steps down to 1.125rem where the title sits inside a sheet (skill groups, learning columns, note titles, engagement h4s).

subtitle.purpose: Panel subtitles, the hero statement (1.25rem, 1.125rem below 640px) and the contact lead.

body.purpose: All prose at a 68ch measure (62ch in About and Education). Tabular numerals on globally so dates align down the timeline column.

small.purpose: Meta lines, dates, notes, the footer.

control.purpose: Buttons, nav links, folder tabs, fact strips. 0.875rem for tabs below 900px. Never the display face.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked row labels only: dt cells, date columns, contact row labels. Never a kicker above a heading.

chip.purpose: Technology names in code chips. Source Code Pro is loaded at 400 only.

status.purpose: The Core / Growing / Completed / In progress tokens sitting inline beside an h3.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: The single elevation in light theme: sheets, panels, project notes, the portrait, the CV page. Warm-tinted brown drawn from the ink, never neutral black.

shadows.name: sheet-edge-dark
shadows.purpose: The same --shadow token redefined in dark theme: a 1px hairline ring stands in for the drop shadow, which would read as smudge on a dark ground.

shadows.name: tab-lift
shadows.purpose: The one upward-cast shadow in the system, on the selected folder tab in light theme, so the tab reads as continuous with the sheet below it. Replaced by the hairline ring in dark.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Colour and opacity state changes: buttons, links, tabs, nav links, the theme toggle, the note chevron, the heading anchor.

motion.name: motion-base
motion.purpose: The sliding nav indicator, the only movement in the system.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single curve. Every transition uses it.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every duration collapses to zero and smooth scrolling is off. The indicator still moves, it just arrives instantly.

breakpoints.name: compact-hero
breakpoints.purpose: Max-width. The 12-column hero grid unstacks: text column and work sheet each take all 12.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Max-width. Header wraps to two rows and --header-height is redefined 4rem to 6.5rem; nav becomes a masked scrolling strip; panel grid, fact strip, skill rows, timeline, learning, About and Contact all go single-column and their vertical dividers become horizontal.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Max-width. The mail button collapses to a 2.75rem circle, contact and field rows stack, section padding drops to 1rem, the hero statement drops to 1.125rem.

breakpoints.name: hint-centre
breakpoints.purpose: Min-width. The CV print hint centres itself instead of hanging left.

layout.name: measure
layout.purpose: Default paragraph cap, applied by the element rule rather than opt-in. 62ch in the About and Education columns.

layout.name: header-height
layout.purpose: Sticky header height and the basis of scroll-padding-top. Redefined to 6.5rem below 900px.

components.description: Terracotta fill behind white. The Get in touch action only, twice on the page.

narrative.overview:
A butter-yellow page, warm enough to read as paper rather than as a screen, with the work laid on a white sheet that sits on top of it. The sheet is the event: it carries folder tabs that rise from its top edge, and the selected tab fuses into the sheet the way a tab fuses into a file folder. Everything else — the identity fields, the skills table, the dated timeline, the expandable project notes — either sits on another sheet or lies directly on the butter ground. Depth in this world is one soft drop of warm shadow under a sheet; there is no second layer, no glass, no gradient.

The tone is calm credibility, not spectacle. The heavy Gabarito headline and the single terracotta accent do the shouting; the rest is warm brown ink on butter at a comfortable 1.0625rem with a 68ch measure. Motion is short (150ms and 220ms) and confined to colour, opacity and one sliding nav underline that animates transform only. One chromatic voice runs the whole surface: terracotta on links, the primary action, the selected tab, the current nav item, the hero rule, list markers and the focus ring. Nothing else is coloured.

The confirmed anti-references are two: the plain black-on-white document look this build replaced, and the dark terminal developer-portfolio template. The system also has to stay recognisably its own against the colleague's reference site that inspired the composition — the composition system carries over, the palette and display face do not.
keyCharacteristics: Butter ground, deeper butter band, warm off-white sheets — three tones of the same warmth.
One accent hue (terracotta), used on roughly a tenth of any screen.
Gabarito 800 headlines set tight (-0.03em at display size) against a calm Source Sans 3 body.
Sheets lifted by a single soft warm shadow in light, by a 1px hairline ring in dark — never both.
Folder tabs on the featured-work sheet as the structural signature.
Full parity across light, dark, print, no-JavaScript and 320px.

rules.name: The One Terracotta Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one chromatic hue on this site. If a new element needs colour to be understood, it does not need colour — it needs weight, a hairline, or a label.

rules.name: The Two Terracottas Rule
rules.body: #a4441f is terracotta as text on butter; #c4532b is terracotta as a fill behind white. They are not interchangeable and neither may be substituted for the other to “match” — the split exists so both directions clear WCAG AA.

rules.name: The Strong Hairline Is For Controls Rule
rules.body: #8f8058 outlines things you can operate. #e8dcb6 rules things you read. A content divider never uses the strong hairline; a control outline never uses the soft one.

rules.name: The Gabarito-For-Structure Rule
rules.body: Gabarito appears only on things that structure the page: the brand, headings, case and note and column titles. It never sets a paragraph, a button, a chip or a label. Buttons and tabs are Source Sans 3 600 — the display face would make a control look like a headline.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-A-Name Rule
rules.body: Source Code Pro is used where the string is a machine name or a machine state: technology chips, the CV tech lines, status tokens. It is never used for emphasis, for numbers, or for “technical feel”.

rules.name: The Two-Step Headline Rule
rules.body: The h1 is set a step below the case title. The name identifies; the sheet is the event. Any new hero must keep this relationship rather than inflating the h1.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked label only ever appears as the left column of a row — a dt, a date column, a contact-row label. It never sits above a heading as an eyebrow or kicker.

rules.name: The 8px Module Rule
rules.body: Every margin, padding and gap comes from the eight-step scale. A one-off value is a sign the component is wrong, not the scale.

rules.name: The 68ch Measure Rule
rules.body: Paragraphs carry max-width: 68ch by default, not by opt-in. Widening a column never widens its prose.

rules.name: The Elevation Declared Once Rule
rules.body: A surface declares its edge once: a shadow or a hairline, never both. If a component needs a visible border in light theme, it is not a sheet — it is a notice (like the CV print hint, which is bordered and unlifted).

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadow colour is rgba(56, 42, 12, …), a brown drawn from the ink, never rgba(0,0,0,…). A neutral shadow turns the butter grey.

rules.name: The Folded Corner Rule
rules.body: The featured-work panel's top-left corner is square (border-radius: 0 12px 12px 12px) because a tab sits on it. When the tab row is absent — no JavaScript, or a stacked second panel — the panel takes the full 12px on all four corners.

dos: Do keep terracotta to one hue and roughly a tenth of any screen — links, the primary action, the current nav item, the selected tab, the hero rule, list markers, focus.
Do use #a4441f for terracotta text on butter and #c4532b only as a fill behind white.
Do declare a surface's edge once: the sheet lift in light, the hairline ring in dark, never both.
Do alternate sheet and bare ground down the page — a long page of nothing but sheets reads as one slab.
Do set every heading in Gabarito (700/800) and every control, label and paragraph in Source Sans 3.
Do reserve Source Code Pro for technology names and status tokens.
Do take every margin, padding and gap from the eight-step 8px scale.
Do cap prose at 68ch (62ch in the About and Education columns).
Do ship enhanced behaviour hidden: the tab row is display: none and the theme toggle is hidden until JavaScript wires them.
Do draw icons as inline SVG with aria-hidden="true" and a text or aria-label name beside them.
Do give interactive targets a minimum height of 2.75rem.
Do use --border-strong for control outlines and --border for content rules.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, a gradient, a tinted glass surface or a second elevation level.
Don't use a neutral black shadow — shadow colour is rgba(56, 42, 12, …).
Don't put a visible border and a shadow on the same surface.
Don't set Gabarito on a paragraph, a button, a chip or a label, and don't inflate the h1 past the case title.
Don't place an uppercase tracked label above a heading as a kicker or eyebrow — labels are row labels.
Don't render a dense taxonomy as chips; chips are for a stack of about five.
Don't animate layout properties. The nav indicator moves on transform only.
Don't add semantics in markup that JavaScript has to make true — no role="tab" on a row that cannot be operated without script.
Don't let the print stylesheet inherit screen colour, shadow or chrome; print is black on white with no world.
Don't add an external resource beyond Google Fonts.
